scenes.title: 문 하나가 바꾸는 질문
lines: A character stands by a switch and presses it. The door opens. In Unreal Engine, developers have built interactions like this by wiring nodes together in Blueprints. Epic Games now plans to retire this system in Unreal Engine 6. Where will we put the rule that opens the door?

scenes.title: 도쿄 발표의 세 항목
lines: At the Tokyo presentation on November 3, 2026, three items appeared together: Actors, Blueprints and the C++ Gameplay Framework. Read that last name in full. C++ continues to power engine systems such as rendering and physics. The change concerns the gameplay code that decides what happens when someone presses the switch.

scenes.title: 지금은 어떻게 연결할까
lines: In Unreal Engine 5, a door and a switch are objects you can place in a level. Unreal calls these objects Actors. Components on an Actor can supply its visible shape or its collision volume. Press the switch with a key and the door opens. Without a key, it stays shut. Blueprints express that condition and its outcomes as connected nodes.

scenes.title: 액터에서 캐릭터까지
lines: The character opening the door has the same roots. Look at the actual UE5 class declarations. Character inherits from Pawn, and Pawn inherits from Actor. Inheritance lets a class build on the abilities of its parent. A player or AI can control a Pawn. Character adds support for actions such as walking and jumping. Developers extend these building blocks with their own behaviors. Together, they form part of the Gameplay Framework.

scenes.title: 같은 문을 새 구조에 놓으면
lines: Epic calls the new framework Scene Graph. An Entity is a unit in the scene. Components supply what it displays and how it behaves. Build our door again. Give the door Entity a visible shape, interaction detection and a behavior that checks for a key. Make the door leaf a child Entity so it can turn around the hinge. Move the parent and the entire door moves. Rotate the child and just the leaf swings open.

scenes.title: 규칙은 Verse로
lines: Write the key check in Verse, Epic's programming language. The difference looks small with one door. It matters more when a team has a hundred doors using the same rule. Save that structure as a prefab, a template that can be placed repeatedly, and its behavior can be reused. You can already try Verse and Scene Graph in Unreal Editor for Fortnite, known as UEFN.

scenes.title: 6월과 11월의 차이
lines: Epic outlined the new framework in June. Its roadmap at the time called for Actors and Blueprints to ship in early UE6 versions, with a gradual phaseout once the new framework matured. The Tokyo presentation in November changed that sequence. Removal is now planned from Early Access, the first public development release. That changes when a team can try both approaches side by side during a migration.

scenes.title: 왜 텍스트와 AI인가
lines: Epic cited development speed and portability. Portability means that behavior or content made in one project is easier to use in another. AI tools are part of that plan. Epic reported internal productivity ranging from one and a half to four times its previous level across programming, debugging and level design. Those figures describe Epic's own observations.

scenes.title: 개발자가 맡길 일을 고른다
lines: Imagine checking a hundred doors for a missing key requirement. A developer can write the rule, have a tool search for exceptions, then inspect the results. Model Context Protocol, or MCP, connects an AI tool to functions exposed by the editor. Python offers a way to script repetitive tasks. Writing the rule the door follows and choosing a tool to inspect it are two separate decisions.

scenes.title: 옮길 때 무엇을 확인할까
lines: What happens to a door already built in Blueprints? Epic has announced AI-assisted conversion, with the delivery format still open. Epic is also migrating existing Blueprints and gameplay code in Fortnite while the service operates. For our simple door, try two interactions before and after the move. Does it stay closed without a key? Does it open once the player has one? Those two outcomes define the behavior to preserve.

scenes.title: 5.9와 6의 시계
lines: A game that already delivers those results reliably can continue development on UE5. On November 3, Epic announced that the UE5.9 preview was planned for the following week. Announced features include web as a target platform, improved AI workflows, and rendering and animation updates. The UE6 Early Access target is late 2027. These dates refer to two different releases.

scenes.title: 지금 배우는 사람에게
lines: If you are learning Unreal now, try finishing one door before UE6 arrives. Decide what counts as input, which condition to check and what the player should see. Then try expressing the same door with Entities and Verse in UEFN. The door still opens on screen, and you can now identify exactly which parts of its implementation have to move.

scenes.title: 이래도 언리얼을 선택할까?
lines: Rebuilding the same door leaves one question. If Blueprints were the reason you chose Unreal, would you still choose it after this change? All three engines can build this door. The choice depends on what is outside it. Say you already have dozens of maps and characters in Unreal, and your team knows its lighting and animation tools. That is a good reason to finish the game in UE5. Even for a new game, if you intend to publish inside Fortnite, building and playtesting in UEFN fits that goal. A team building its first room can consider Godot and Unity from the start.

scenes.title: 고도는 상용 게임도 무료
lines: In Godot, group the door leaf and switch as nodes in a scene. When the switch emits a signal, GDScript on the door can check the key and rotate the leaf. Godot has a clear advantage here. The engine is free. There is no engine fee per developer as the team grows, and game sales do not trigger engine royalties. Godot also publishes its engine source under the MIT license. When shipping the engine with your game, include its copyright and license notice in your credits or documentation.

scenes.title: 유니티는 팀과 좌석을 본다
lines: In Unity, create a GameObject for the door. Attach a C# script as a component to implement the same rule. If your team knows C# and already owns suitable Unity assets, that can shorten the time to a first playable room. Pricing depends on the team's finances over the last 12 months. For a team making its own game, combined revenue and funding of up to $200,000 qualify for free Unity Personal. Above that threshold, a team on Unity Pro pays US$2,310 per seat per year on the US prepaid annual plan.

scenes.title: 같은 게임의 엔진 비용
lines: Let's compare all three with one set of numbers. Imagine a two-person team's first PC game, sold only on Steam. Its first quarter takes lifetime gross revenue to $1.2 million. The engine fee payable to Godot is still $0. Two prepaid annual Unity Pro seats cost $4,620. Under Unreal's current standard game royalty terms, the first $1 million in lifetime gross product revenue is excluded. Here, 5% of the remaining $200,000 is $10,000. These figures compare payments to the engine provider. Store fees and labor are separate costs.

scenes.title: 우리 팀에 남는 선택
lines: The Blueprint announcement alone cannot choose an engine for our team. If you have substantial Unreal work, start with the value of that investment. If you can reuse C# code and assets, look at Unity. If you are starting fresh and want zero engine fees and royalties plus the freedom to modify the engine, Godot has a strong case. If you are undecided, build that door and the first room in your two finalists. See how quickly your team can change it and run it again on your target device. That experience will tell you which engine fits your game.
